questions.subtopic: A-R: Majority Community vs Majority Rule
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Rule by majority must not be converted into rule by a majority community based on religion, race, or language.
Reason (R): If rule by majority becomes majoritarian domination, democracy ceases to accommodate minorities and violates fundamental human equality.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

(A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Democratic majority rule means shifting political majorities on issues and elections; when it degenerates into permanent ethnic/religious majoritarianism, democratic accommodation collapses.

questions.subtopic: Case Analysis: Sri Lanka vs Belgium Lesson
questions.question: In 1956, Sri Lanka made Sinhala the sole official language, disregarding Tamil speakers. In contrast, Belgium amended its constitution four times to ensure Dutch and French speakers shared power equally. What fundamental lesson does this offer regarding democratic outcomes?
options: Democracy succeeds only when the majority works with minorities and refrains from majoritarian tyranny
Democracy requires all nations to adopt multilingual currency notes
Authoritarian military dictatorships handle linguistic diversity better than democracies
Small nations should never conduct parliamentary elections
questions.explanation: Belgium accommodated diversity by sharing power; Sri Lanka imposed majoritarianism which provoked civil war. Democracy requires majorities to cooperate with minorities.
